role: Detects when a current metric value deviates significantly from its established baseline, using real statistical z-score analysis rather than an ML model (no training infrastructure exists in this repo — this is the honest, verifiable version of the same underlying capability).
behaviorDescription: detectDeviation() computes a baseline's mean and sample standard deviation (Bessel's correction) from historical numeric observations already in hand, then scores a current value via z-score, flagging an anomaly when the deviation exceeds a configurable sigma threshold (default 3). Handles a zero-variance (perfectly flat) baseline explicitly rather than dividing by zero, and refuses to compute a baseline from fewer than 2 samples rather than producing a meaningless standard deviation. monitorLiveMetric() is an honest stub: it throws a clear error, because @platform/observability only exposes write-side OTel instruments with no query capability, and no metrics-backend connection exists in this repo to pull real historical values from.
hardStops: Never fabricates a baseline from fewer than 2 samples — refuses rather than producing a meaningless or divide-by-zero result
Never silently treats a zero-variance baseline as 'no anomaly possible' — any different value against a perfectly flat baseline is correctly flagged
monitorLiveMetric() never fakes a metrics-backend query — it throws until a real query capability exists
